text: Tell me, what is it you plan to do with your one wild and precious life?
author: Mary Oliver

text: You do not have to be good. You do not have to walk on your knees for a hundred miles through the desert repenting.
author: Mary Oliver

text: Pay attention. Be astonished. Tell about it.
author: Mary Oliver

text: When it's over, I want to say: all my life I was a bride married to amazement.
author: Mary Oliver

text: Keep some room in your heart for the unimaginable.
author: Mary Oliver

text: Someone I loved once gave me a box full of darkness. It took me years to understand that this too, was a gift.
author: Mary Oliver

text: Let me keep my distance, always, from those who think they have the answers.
author: Mary Oliver

text: If you suddenly and unexpectedly feel joy, don't hesitate. Give in to it.
author: Mary Oliver

text: Joy is not made to be a crumb.
author: Mary Oliver

text: You only have to let the soft animal of your body love what it loves.
author: Mary Oliver

text: One day you finally knew what you had to do, and began.
author: Mary Oliver

text: Out beyond ideas of wrongdoing and rightdoing, there is a field. I'll meet you there.
author: Rumi

text: The wound is the place where the light enters you.
author: Rumi

text: What you seek is seeking you.
author: Rumi

text: Yesterday I was clever, so I wanted to change the world. Today I am wise, so I am changing myself.
author: Rumi

text: Be a lamp, or a lifeboat, or a ladder. Help someone's soul heal.
author: Rumi

text: Respond to every call that excites your spirit.
author: Rumi

text: Don't grieve. Anything you lose comes round in another form.
author: Rumi

text: There is a voice that doesn't use words. Listen.
author: Rumi

text: Sell your cleverness and buy bewilderment.
author: Rumi

text: Let silence take you to the core of life.
author: Rumi

text: You are not a drop in the ocean. You are the entire ocean in a drop.
author: Rumi

text: Your task is not to seek for love, but merely to seek and find all the barriers within yourself that you have built against it.
author: Rumi

text: Be patient toward all that is unsolved in your heart and try to love the questions themselves.
author: Rainer Maria Rilke

text: Let everything happen to you, beauty and terror. Just keep going. No feeling is final.
author: Rainer Maria Rilke

text: The only journey is the one within.
author: Rainer Maria Rilke

text: I live my life in widening circles that reach out across the world.
author: Rainer Maria Rilke

text: Perhaps all the dragons in our lives are princesses who are only waiting to see us act, just once, with beauty and courage.
author: Rainer Maria Rilke

text: I hold this to be the highest task for a bond between two people: that each protects the solitude of the other.
author: Rainer Maria Rilke

text: You are the sky. Everything else — it's just the weather.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: Nothing ever goes away until it has taught us what we need to know.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: We think that the point is to pass the test or overcome the problem, but the truth is that things don't really get solved. They come together and they fall apart.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: Compassion is not a relationship between the healer and the wounded. It's a relationship between equals.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: We already have everything we need.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: Things falling apart is a kind of testing and also a kind of healing.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: The present moment always will have been.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
author: Annie Dillard

text: You were made and set here to give voice to this, your own astonishment.
author: Annie Dillard

text: The secret of seeing is to sail on solar wind. Hone and spread your spirit till you yourself are a sail, whetted, translucent, broadside to the merest puff.
author: Annie Dillard

text: It may be that when we no longer know what to do, we have come to our real work, and when we no longer know which way to go, we have begun our real journey.
author: Wendell Berry

text: Ask the questions that have no answers. Invest in the millennium. Plant sequoias.
author: Wendell Berry

text: It is not from ourselves that we learn to be better than we are.
author: Wendell Berry

text: The real work of planet-saving will be small, humble, and humbling.
author: Wendell Berry

text: The present moment is the only moment available to us, and it is the door to all moments.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: Sometimes the most important thing in a whole day is the rest we take between two deep breaths.
author: Etty Hillesum

text: Drink your tea slowly and reverently, as if it is the axis on which the world revolves — slowly, completely, without hurry.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: The most precious gift we can offer anyone is our attention.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: Peace is present right here and now, in ourselves and in everything we do and see.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: Smile, breathe, and go slowly.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: Because you are alive, everything is possible.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: Walk as if you are kissing the earth with your feet.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: The antidote to exhaustion is not necessarily rest. The antidote to exhaustion is wholeheartedness.
author: David Whyte

text: Start close in, don't take the second step or the third, start with the first thing close in, the step you don't want to take.
author: David Whyte

text: To be human is to become visible while carrying what is hidden as a gift to others.
author: David Whyte

text: You must learn one thing: the world was made to be free in.
author: David Whyte

text: May you awaken to the mystery of being here and enter the quiet immensity of your own presence.
author: John O'Donohue

text: May you experience each day as a sacred gift woven around the heart of wonder.
author: John O'Donohue

text: At the end of the day, let there be no excuses, no explanations, no regrets.
author: John O'Donohue

text: Even after all this time, the sun never says to the earth, 'You owe me.' Look what happens with a love like that — it lights the whole sky.
author: Hafiz

text: I wish I could show you, when you are lonely or in darkness, the astonishing light of your own being.
author: Hafiz

text: Now that all your worry has proved such an unlucrative business, why not find a better job?
author: Hafiz

text: Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.
author: Simone Weil

text: If the only prayer you ever say in your entire life is thank you, it will be enough.
author: Meister Eckhart

text: The soul speaks its truth only under quiet, inviting, and trustworthy conditions.
author: Parker Palmer

text: Before I can tell my life what I want to do with it, I must listen to my life telling me who I am.
author: Parker Palmer

text: Self-care is never a selfish act — it is simply good stewardship of the only gift I have, the gift I was put on earth to offer others.
author: Parker Palmer

text: I am large, I contain multitudes.
author: Walt Whitman

text: I believe a leaf of grass is no less than the journey-work of the stars.
author: Walt Whitman

text: Henceforth I ask not good fortune — I myself am good fortune.
author: Walt Whitman

text: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
author: Laozi

text: Nature does not hurry, yet everything is accomplished.
author: Laozi

text: To the mind that is still, the whole universe surrenders.
author: Laozi

text: When I let go of what I am, I become what I might be.
author: Laozi

text: Knowing others is wisdom; knowing yourself is enlightenment.
author: Laozi

text: Do not be too timid and squeamish about your actions. All life is an experiment.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Finish each day and be done with it. You have done what you could.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: The cure for anything is salt water: sweat, tears, or the sea.
author: Isak Dinesen

text: We shall not cease from exploration, and the end of all our exploring will be to arrive where we started and know the place for the first time.
author: T.S. Eliot

text: Wherever you are is called Here, and you must treat it as a powerful stranger.
author: David Wagoner

text: The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Confine yourself to the present.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Nowhere can man find a quieter or more untroubled retreat than in his own soul.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: When you wake up in the morning, think of what a precious privilege it is to be alive — to breathe, to think, to enjoy, to love.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: We suffer more in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca

text: Begin at once to live, and count each day as a separate life.
author: Seneca

text: Don't explain your philosophy. Embody it.
author: Epictetus

text: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
author: Epictetus

text: Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens.
author: Epictetus

text: He is a wise man who does not grieve for the things which he has not, but rejoices for those which he has.
author: Epictetus

text: The meaning of life is just to be alive. It is so plain and so obvious and so simple.
author: Alan Watts

text: The only way to make sense out of change is to plunge into it, move with it, and join the dance.
author: Alan Watts

text: Muddy water is best cleared by leaving it alone.
author: Alan Watts

text: You are under no obligation to be the same person you were five minutes ago.
author: Alan Watts

text: In the beginner's mind there are many possibilities, but in the expert's mind there are few.
author: Shunryu Suzuki

text: Each of you is perfect the way you are... and you can use a little improvement.
author: Shunryu Suzuki

text: Without accepting the fact that everything changes, we cannot find perfect composure.
author: Shunryu Suzuki

text: When you do something, you should burn yourself completely, like a good bonfire, leaving no trace of yourself.
author: Shunryu Suzuki

text: Faith is the bird that feels the light when the dawn is still dark.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The butterfly counts not months but moments, and has time enough.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: I slept and dreamt that life was joy. I awoke and saw that life was service. I acted and behold, service was joy.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Let your life lightly dance on the edges of time like dew on the tip of a leaf.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: You can't cross the sea merely by standing and staring at the water.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Your pain is the breaking of the shell that encloses your understanding.
author: Kahlil Gibran

text: The deeper that sorrow carves into your being, the more joy you can contain.
author: Kahlil Gibran

text: Trust in dreams, for in them is the hidden gate to eternity.
author: Kahlil Gibran

text: Beauty is not in the face; beauty is a light in the heart.
author: Kahlil Gibran

text: Between stimulus and response there is a space. In that space is our power to choose our response. In our response lies our growth and our freedom.
author: Viktor Frankl

text: Those who have a 'why' to live can bear with almost any 'how'.
author: Viktor Frankl

text: When we are no longer able to change a situation, we are challenged to change ourselves.
author: Viktor Frankl

text: It is good to have an end to journey toward; but it is the journey that matters, in the end.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: Love doesn't just sit there, like a stone, it has to be made, like bread; remade all the time, made new.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: The creative adult is the child who survived.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: All that you touch, you change. All that you change, changes you.
author: Octavia Butler

text: Don't ask what the world needs. Ask what makes you come alive, and go do it. Because what the world needs is people who have come alive.
author: Howard Thurman

text: There is something in every one of you that waits and listens for the sound of the genuine in yourself.
author: Howard Thurman

text: My mission in life is not merely to survive, but to thrive; and to do so with some passion, some compassion, some humor, and some style.
author: Maya Angelou

text: We delight in the beauty of the butterfly, but rarely admit the changes it has gone through to achieve that beauty.
author: Maya Angelou

text: Nothing can dim the light that shines from within.
author: Maya Angelou

text: Try to be a rainbow in someone's cloud.
author: Maya Angelou

text: You can't use up creativity. The more you use, the more you have.
author: Maya Angelou

text: Not everything that is faced can be changed, but nothing can be changed until it is faced.
author: James Baldwin

text: Love takes off the masks that we fear we cannot live without and know we cannot live within.
author: James Baldwin

text: You are your best thing.
author: Toni Morrison

text: If you have some power, then your job is to empower somebody else.
author: Toni Morrison

text: The function of freedom is to free someone else.
author: Toni Morrison

text: Knowing how to be solitary is central to the art of loving.
author: bell hooks

text: Tenderness and care do not make us weak; they enlarge our capacity to be fully human.
author: bell hooks

text: There are years that ask questions and years that answer.
author: Zora Neale Hurston

text: Love makes your soul crawl out from its hiding place.
author: Zora Neale Hurston

text: No matter how far a person can go, the horizon is still way beyond you.
author: Zora Neale Hurston

text: Hold fast to dreams, for if dreams die, life is a broken-winged bird that cannot fly.
author: Langston Hughes

text: Life is for the living. Death is for the dead. Let life be like music, and death a note unsaid.
author: Langston Hughes

text: At the end of the day, we can endure much more than we think we can.
author: Frida Kahlo

text: I paint flowers so they will not die.
author: Frida Kahlo

text: Feet, what do I need them for if I have wings to fly?
author: Frida Kahlo

text: Hope is not a lottery ticket you can sit on the sofa and clutch, feeling lucky. It is an axe you break down doors with in an emergency.
author: Rebecca Solnit

text: Leave the door open for the unknown, the door into the dark.
author: Rebecca Solnit

text: The world is blue at its edges and in its depths.
author: Rebecca Solnit

text: Art enables us to find ourselves and lose ourselves at the same time.
author: Thomas Merton

text: The biggest human temptation is to settle for too little.
author: Thomas Merton

text: Happiness is not a matter of intensity but of balance, order, rhythm and harmony.
author: Thomas Merton

text: To see a world in a grain of sand and heaven in a wild flower, hold infinity in the palm of your hand and eternity in an hour.
author: William Blake

text: No bird soars too high if he soars with his own wings.
author: William Blake

text: Think in the morning. Act in the noon. Eat in the evening. Sleep in the night.
author: William Blake

text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: You must live in the present, launch yourself on every wave, find your eternity in each moment.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Wealth is the ability to fully experience life.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: You cannot find peace by avoiding life.
author: Virginia Woolf

text: Arrange whatever pieces come your way.
author: Virginia Woolf

text: Change your life today. Don't gamble on the future, act now, without delay.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

text: I wish that every human life might be pure transparent freedom.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

text: Ultimately, we have just one moral duty: to reclaim large areas of peace in ourselves, more and more peace, and to reflect it toward others.
author: Etty Hillesum

text: Before you know kindness as the deepest thing inside, you must know sorrow as the other deepest thing.
author: Naomi Shihab Nye

text: This world of dew is only a world of dew — and yet... and yet...
author: Kobayashi Issa

text: In this world we walk on the roof of hell, gazing at flowers.
author: Kobayashi Issa

text: What a strange thing! to be alive beneath cherry blossoms.
author: Kobayashi Issa

text: Even in Kyoto, hearing the cuckoo, I long for Kyoto.
author: Matsuo Bashō

text: Every day is a little life: every waking and rising a little birth, every fresh morning a little youth.
author: Arthur Schopenhauer

text: The moment one definitely commits oneself, then Providence moves too.
author: W.H. Murray
